title: Win32 function map
description: One file per DLL per target: what that target needs from a Windows DLL, and how the host answers it.

kind.description: shim: the host must answer these calls. inventory: a record of usage, for a port that replaces the platform layer instead.

dll.description: DLL name as the guest imports it, e.g. KERNEL32.dll

target.description: Which game/profile this map belongs to, e.g. doraemon-monopoly-1998

dll.description: Only when this entry belongs to a different DLL than the file's.

object.description: COM interface this method belongs to (IDirectDraw, IDirectDrawSurface7, IUnknown...). Such a method has no import slot: the guest reaches it through its vtable, which the host dispatches separately. Entries with an object are documented, not emitted into the import table.

rust_name.description: Override the generated Rust identifier. Needed where the project already chose a name that is not a plain snake_case of the Win32 name (CreateWindowExA -> create_window_ex).

args.description: Declared signature, for documentation and arg_bytes estimation.

arg_bytes.description: Bytes of arguments the callee pops. Authoritative: the session cross-checks it against the dispatch table.

status.description: inventory maps: what the port currently does about this call.

replaced_by.description: inventory maps: file/symbol that takes over this behaviour in a source port.

description.description: Why this entry exists, in terms of the game's behaviour.

evidence.description: Trace line, call count, or source call site that proved the requirement.

value.description: For kind=return: the Rust expression to return, e.g. "0" or "WINDOWS_VERSION".

body.description: For kind=custom: a verbatim Rust body. Must return Result<Action>.

reason.description: For kind=unimplemented: what the run should print when the guest reaches it.
